expectations.text: Claude confirms the reviewer is correct — TWFE with staggered adoption and heterogeneous treatment effects can be biased even when parallel trends holds for every cohort
expectations.evidence: Response opens with 'Your reviewer is correct' and explicitly states 'Critically: this happens even when parallel trends holds perfectly for every cohort. It's not a parallel trends violation — it's a mechanical artifact of how TWFE constructs weights under staggered timing.' Reinforced again in Section 7: 'This is not a parallel trends violation — it's a weighting problem that occurs even when parallel trends holds for every cohort.'

expectations.text: Claude explains the core mechanism: TWFE uses already-treated units as controls for later-treated units ('forbidden comparisons'), which is only unbiased if treatment effects are constant across cohorts and over time
expectations.evidence: Section 3 explains: 'the control group for each cohort isn't just clean never-treated units — it includes already-treated regions from earlier cohorts.' The Late vs. Early comparison is described as contaminated. The constant-effects condition is stated: 'If the program has a constant, immediate effect that doesn't change with exposure duration, TWFE is unbiased.'

expectations.text: Claude names or describes the Goodman-Bacon decomposition problem — that TWFE is a weighted average of 2×2 DiDs, some receiving negative weights when later-cohort treatment effects differ from early-cohort effects
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly names 'the Goodman-Bacon (2021) decomposition' and explains 'the TWFE coefficient is a weighted average of all pairwise 2x2 DiD comparisons.' Negative weights are described in Section 7: 'can include negative weights on valid treatment effects when the effect is dynamic, because already-treated units are used as implicit controls for later-adopting cohorts.'

expectations.text: Claude recommends a heterogeneity-robust DiD estimator (e.g., Callaway-Sant'Anna, Sun-Abraham, or Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess) rather than standard TWFE
expectations.evidence: Section 5 recommends Callaway & Sant'Anna (2021) as the 'Recommended Starting Point' and Sun & Abraham (2021) as Option B. Section 7 commits to 'Running Callaway-Sant'Anna or Sun-Abraham estimates before presenting conclusions.' The quick reference table also lists both estimators with implementation packages.
